comment: The single source of truth for the CI-gate vulnerability-scanner set.
A candidate is clean when every scanner in this list says so; policy
and docs read this list and never hard-code a scanner count or name.
Decision register row 45 (Sep 21, owner's line in the sand, amending
row 44): the CI gate is TWO scanners, Grype + OSV-Scanner. Trivy left
the CI gate (three scanners is too much CI time for one developer).
- grype        : Anchore's vulnerability database (its own aggregation
and matcher). Primary, on the owner's binary benchmark.
Scans the OCI images (both platform children) and every
release archive.
- osv-scanner  : the OSV.dev database (osv-scalibr; deps.dev), a
different aggregation and implementation. Scans the
two OCI images (production and -fips) on both architectures
(four children)
AND the Go modules.
These are two scanners with DIFFERENT DATABASES (different aggregations
and implementations) built on OVERLAPPING upstream advisory sources -
OSV imports the GitHub Advisory and Go Vulnerability databases, which
Grype also consumes - so this is 'different databases', NOT 'different
sources', and scanner disagreement is an investigation signal, never
proof of a false positive. The daily main-candidate rescan is a separate
set of four (Grype, Docker Scout, Amazon Inspector, Google Artifact
Analysis; Trivy and Snyk are removed from the rescan, scanner-panel rules
of Oct 2, rule 1) and is NOT this list; the daily rescan of the published
release (same workflow) still reads 'scanners' from this file.
Row 57 (owner, Sep 24; part B, Sep 28): the PR GATE (scan.yml) is its own
list, `pr_gate`: Grype + Amazon Inspector (inspector-sbomgen SBOM sent to
inspector-scan:ScanSbom by OIDC role assumption; no stored secret). Trivy
and OSV-Scanner leave the PR gate; govulncheck stays the Go authority.
`source_scanners` (advisor Oct 12, ruling G): the Go source scan of the release chain's
Check stage, run once on the tagged checkout by bin/check-govulncheck.py; its
stream is a product of the scanners record that Release binds and hands to the
dependency evidence step. It is not a per-image scanner, so it is not in `scanners`.
`scanners` above is unchanged: it still drives the release chain
(the Check stage, stage-verify.yml), the rescans and the daily auditor's
candidate, until the candidate-panel handoff moves them.
